items.t: The page is about the board sub-area "Brookswood" in the Township of Langley, BC, inside the Brookswood-Fernridge community area (Booth, Fernridge and Rinn neighbourhood plans), framed entirely through development potential after the Township's 2024 SSMUH rezoning.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Brookswood Real Estate Development Guide

items.t: SSMUH, Township Bylaw 6020: Bylaw No. 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024) amended Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 to allow small-scale multi-unit housing on eligible lots (inside the Urban Containment Boundary, connected to municipal water and sewer, no heritage designation, not in a Transit Oriented Area, lot not larger than 4,050 m²). Eligible lots of 280 m² or smaller can have 3 units, larger eligible lots can have 4 units, lots over 4,050 m² are ineligible, and no six-unit tier currently applies in the Township.

Zoning and lot sizes: Township Zoning Bylaw 1987 No. 2500 zones named in Township notices for the area include SR-1, SR-2, SR-3 and RU-2. Read from Bylaw 2500 Section 110.1 in Township council reports: SR-1 minimum lot area 3,716 m² and minimum frontage 40 m; SR-2 minimum 8,094 m² and 45 m; SR-3 minimum 1,765 m² and 27.45 m. RU-2 minimum lot area and frontage are not verified from a readable bylaw section.

Presales (REDMA) — the frame for every developer sale named here: REDMA s. 21 gives a 7-day rescission period from the later of signing and acknowledging the disclosure statement, with deposits held in trust under s. 18. Bromley is selling as a presale with Phase 1 completion estimated Summer 2027 on the developer's sheet, so developer contracts there sit inside this frame.

ALR / second dwellings: the Agricultural Land Commission's housing rules permit one principal residence and, subject to conditions in the ALR Use Regulation, one additional residence, limited to 90 m² or less on parcels 40 ha or smaller and 186 m² or less on parcels larger than 40 ha. Township zoning for a second dwelling or coach house on non-reserve Brookswood acreage is not verified. ALR residences cannot be stratified, so ALR parcels never become condo stock.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Brookswood Real Estate Development Guide

items.t: SSMUH — Township Bylaw 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024): 3 units on lots up to 280 m² and 4 units on larger eligible lots under 4,050 m²; eligibility requires the Urban Containment Boundary, municipal water and sewer, no heritage designation, and the lot must not be in a Transit Oriented Area; lots over 4,050 m² are ineligible. Bylaw 6020 has no six-unit tier.

ALR block (parcel status in Brookswood is parcel-specific and not verified here; this page's blanket statement that "ALR properties are excluded entirely" is carried as page copy only, without the parcel-level caution): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)). Caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error.

faq.a: A fourplex, possibly: under Bylaw No. 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024), an eligible lot (inside the Urban Containment Boundary, on municipal water and sewer, no heritage designation, not in a Transit Oriented Area, 4,050 m² or smaller) permits 4 units if it is over 280 m² and 3 units at 280 m² or smaller. A sixplex is not available: the Township bylaw has no six-unit tier. Some Brookswood lots are still on septic, so confirm servicing first.
faq.q: Can I build a fourplex — or a sixplex — on my Brookswood lot?

faq.a: Treat them as leads to verify with the Township, not as approvals.
faq.q: The page names a 60-unit project and a 37-lot subdivision — can I price against them?

faq.a: No. Bylaw 6020 allows 3 units at 280 m² or less and 4 units up to 4,050 m² on eligible lots. Transit Oriented Area lots are not eligible, and the Township has no six-unit tier.
faq.q: Can I build six homes on a Brookswood lot near transit?

faq.a: A strata townhouse presale at 4558 208 Street by Leone Homes — 26 customizable townhomes, Phase 1 estimated Summer 2027.
The duplex form here is the individual duplex on a single lot under the zoning of its day, and the SSMUH two-unit baseline on an eligible lot.
faq.q: Is there a duplex development in Brookswood I can buy into?

faq.a: No — per the disk they are pad-rental leasehold non-strata parks, documented at their Brookswood mobile homes. You would own the home as a chattel and rent the pad; you would not own land, and the mhpta — not the Strata Property Act — governs.
faq.q: Are Cedar Creek Estates or Fernridge Park bare-land strata?

faq.a: Match the lot to the zone minimums first: SR-1 needs 3,716 m², SR-2 needs 8,094 m² and SR-3 needs 1,765 m² under Bylaw 2500 Section 110.1 in Township council reports; RU-2 minimums could not be confirmed from the bylaw.
faq.q: What lot size do I need to subdivide?

faq.a: Possibly — under Bylaw No. 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024), an eligible lot (inside the Urban Containment Boundary, on municipal water and sewer, no heritage designation, not in a Transit Oriented Area, 4,050 m² or smaller) permits 4 units if it is over 280 m² and 3 units at 280 m² or smaller. There is no 6-unit tier in the Township, whatever a listing or guide says about transit-adjacent lots.
faq.q: Can I build a fourplex on my Brookswood lot?

faq.a: The Brookswood-Fernridge Community Plan, with the Booth, Fernridge and Rinn Neighbourhood Plans under it; the Township states the plan allows previously undeveloped areas to grow while protecting trees and watercourses.

Some Township properties are in the Agricultural Land Reserve and some are not; check the exact parcel on the Agricultural Land Commission map and in the Township's GeoSource before making any development assumption — ALC rules permit one additional residence on ALR land only within its size caps and subject to Township bylaws.
